summary: Preinstall dropper fetches Bun runtime and executes obfuscated 728KB bundled payload
details: @servicetitan/contentful-proxy 1.1.17 declares scripts.preinstall = 'node setup.mjs'. setup.mjs downloads the Bun runtime (bun-v1.3.13) from oven-sh/bun GitHub releases into a temp directory, chmods it executable, and invokes it against a sibling file math_init.js. math_init.js is a 727,680-byte '// @bun @bun-cjs' compiled bundle using string-array rotation obfuscation (WV8StW shifter over a ~1000-entry mixed number/string dictionary), hex-name identifiers, and no readable literals. Bun is not a build dependency of a Contentful/React helper library, and there is no legitimate reason to fetch a second language runtime at install time to hand it an opaque bundle. The package is published under the @servicetitan scope with a plausible-internal name (contentful-proxy) and ships an NSwag-generated React/Contentful body in dist/ and src/ as cover, matching the shape of a scope / dependency-confusion attack targeting ServiceTitan internal builds. dist/contentful/api/contentful.api.client.js also contains network+command patterns flagged by the exfiltration rule. The alternate-runtime dropper executes attacker-controlled, unauditable code on every npm install.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
